prompt: After 30 days of daily practice, Sam's new habit still needs effort, and he concludes he has 'failed at habit-building' because habits are supposed to form in 21 days. What is the most accurate correction?

options.text: He is right: a habit not automatic by day 21 will never form
Habits form in exactly 66 days for everyone, so he should just wait
Research on everyday habits found automaticity took weeks to many months, with wide variation, so needing effort at day 30 is normal, not failure
Effort after 30 days means he picked the wrong habit

explanation: The 21-day figure is a popular myth. Studies of real habits show a broad range of times to automaticity, so steady repetition beyond a month is expected.
